report.source_text: Although the patient was hypovolaemic, this was considered unlikely as a cause for his confusion. Also, his confusion remained after volume resuscitation. Further blood investigation revealed a normal calcium, thyroid-stimulating hormone and only a slight hyponatraemia and hypokalaemia of respectively 130 mmol/L and 3.4 mmol/L, all of which could not explain his neurological status. Sepsis was considered unlikely, since blood cultures remained negative, blood pressure was within normal limits and serum lactate levels were normal. The patient had no history of substance abuse or intoxications.

report.source_text: After the negative PCR results of the CSF acyclovir was stopped. The disturbances in fluid and electrolyte balance were treated with fluid resuscitation and potassium supplementation. Volume repletion was achieved quickly. The patient’s neurological status recovered within 36 hours after the start of ceftriaxone intravenously. Normalisation of sodium levels occurred within 24 hours and potassium levels normalised within 48 hours, after which fluid resuscitation was stopped.

clinician.trajectory_summary: A 45-year-old man presented with acute encephalopathy (lethargy, confusion, disorientation, diminished speech), fever, and diarrhea. Initial workup revealed elevated CRP, leukopenia, and elevated creatinine. Brain CT was normal, ruling out structural causes. Stool culture confirmed Shigella flexneri, sensitive to ceftriaxone. CSF analysis showed mild pleocytosis but was negative for bacterial culture and common viral pathogens. Other potential causes for encephalopathy, such as hypovolemia, electrolyte imbalances, sepsis, substance abuse, and HIV, were ruled out. The patient's neurological status significantly improved within 36 hours after initiation of intravenous ceftriaxone.

key_supporting_evidence.claim: Patient presented with acute encephalopathy, fever, and diarrhea.
Stool culture confirmed Shigella flexneri, sensitive to ceftriaxone.
CSF analysis showed mild pleocytosis but was negative for bacterial culture and common viral pathogens (enterovirus, HSV 1/2, VZV).
Brain CT scan showed no sign of cerebral bleeding or hydrocephalus.
Other causes for confusion, including hypovolemia, electrolyte imbalances, sepsis, and substance abuse, were considered unlikely.
Neurological status recovered within 36 hours after the start of intravenous ceftriaxone.
